problems.title: Split Linked List in Parts
problems.description: Split a linked list into k consecutive parts whose lengths differ by at most one. Earlier parts receive any extra nodes.
problems.constraints: The input list has at least 0 and at most 1000 nodes; k is positive.

occurrences.sourceRef: 09/01/26 Tues, Cappy Spring Line (linked-list partition prompt)

python.code:
class Solution:
    def splitListToParts(self, head: ListNode | None, k: int) -> list[ListNode | None]:
        n = 0; node = head
        while node: n += 1; node = node.next
        base, extra = divmod(n, k); parts = []; node = head
        for i in range(k):
            parts.append(node)
            size = base + (i < extra)
            for _ in range(size - 1): node = node.next
            if node: following=node.next; node.next=None; node=following
        return parts

long minEnergy(int n,int[][] edges,int k){List<int[]>[]g=new List[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g[i]=new ArrayList<>();for(int[]e:edges){g[e[0]].add(new int[]{e[1],e[2],e[3]});g[e[1]].add(new int[]{e[0],e[2],e[3]});}long[][]d=new long[n][k+1];for(long[]row:d)Arrays.fill(row,Long.MAX_VALUE);d[0][0]=0;PriorityQueue<long[]>q=new PriorityQueue<>(Comparator.comparingLong(a->a[0]));q.add(new long[]{0,0,0});while(!q.isEmpty()){long[]x=q.poll();long cost=x[0];int u=(int)x[1],used=(int)x[2];if(cost!=d[u][used])continue;for(int[]e:g[u]){relax(e[0],used,cost+e[1],d,q);if(e[2]==1&&used<k)relax(e[0],used+1,cost,d,q);}}long ans=Arrays.stream(d[n-1]).min().getAsLong();return ans==Long.MAX_VALUE?-1:ans;}
void relax(int v,int used,long nd,long[][]d,PriorityQueue<long[]>q){if(nd<d[v][used]){d[v][used]=nd;q.add(new long[]{nd,v,used});}}

problems.title: Array Division
problems.description: Split an array into at most k nonempty contiguous parts while minimizing the largest part sum.
problems.constraints: n <= 2*10^5; values are nonnegative; 1 <= k <= n.

difficultyProvenance.reason: CSES task 1085; normalized Medium proposal from binary search on answer. Human review approved Medium for this CappyCode import; retained as a normalized proposal.

occurrences.sourceRef: ICPC Week 6 deck, CSES 1085 Array Division

python.code:
n,k=map(int,input().split());a=list(map(int,input().split()))
lo=max(a);hi=sum(a)
while lo<hi:
 mid=(lo+hi)//2; parts=1;cur=0
 for x in a:
  if cur+x>mid:parts+=1;cur=0
  cur+=x

python.spaceComplexityReason: Stores the input array.

problems.title: Elevated Rails
problems.description: Three disconnected island networks are trees. For each query joining two different islands, report the maximum number of stations on a path between the query stations after adding exactly two rails to connect all islands.
problems.constraints: 3 <= n <= 10^5; q <= 2*10^5; the input is a forest of exactly three trees with n-3 edges.
problems.exampleInput: 12 1; sample forest from the regional statement; query 2 11

difficultyProvenance.reason: Proposed Hard because the regional problem combines tree eccentricities and diameter with independent queries; Human review approved Hard for this CappyCode import; retained as a normalized proposal.

python.timeComplexityReason: Each of the three component trees is traversed a constant number of times; each query is O(1).
python.spaceComplexityReason: Stores the forests, component assignments, tree eccentricities and diameters.

problems.title: Longest Subarray with Sum at Most K
problems.description: Given a nonnegative integer array and K, find the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is at most K.
problems.constraints: Array values are nonnegative; n is the array length.

difficultyProvenance.reason: Proposed Medium because it requires an invariant-preserving sliding window; Human review approved Medium for this CappyCode import; retained as a normalized proposal.

occurrences.sourceRef: ICPC Week 1 deck, new sliding-window problem: longest subarray sum <= K

python.code:
def longest_at_most_k(a,k):
 left=total=best=0
 for right,x in enumerate(a):
  total+=x
  while total>k:total-=a[left];left+=1
  best=max(best,right-left+1)
 return best
python.timeComplexityReason: Each index enters and leaves the window at most once.
python.spaceComplexityReason: Uses scalar window bounds and a running sum.

java.code: static int longestAtMostK(int[] a,int k){int left=0,total=0,best=0;for(int right=0;right<a.length;right++){total+=a[right];while(total>k)total-=a[left++];best=Math.max(best,right-left+1);}return best;}
java.timeComplexityReason: Each index enters and leaves the window at most once.
java.spaceComplexityReason: Uses scalar window bounds and a running sum.
